pr_body:
* Overrides no longer happen for set/get.
* They must be checked with a new function: `ProjectSettings::get_setting_with_override()`.
* GLOBAL_DEF/GLOBAL_GET updated to use the above function.
* The ability to disable feature overrides has been removed since it no longer makes sense.

This change solves many problems:
* General confusion about getting the actual or overriden setting.
* Feature tags available after settings are loaded were being ignored, they are now considered.
* Hacks required for the Project Settings editor to work.

- Fixes #64100.
- Fixes up #64014 and #61908.
- Supersedes #71076.
pr_comments: Removed function to disable, applied fixes and updated docs.

issue_context.title: Project settings feature overrides aren't applied in the editor
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0.dev (5df8eae86292303fefe2d412fb8c04126e7ebe87), 3.x too

### System information

Mageia 9 Linux, x86_64

### Issue description

As found in #64014 and #61908, `.editor` feature overrides added by these PRs don't seem to work, even though `TOOLS_ENABLED` builds do define the `editor` feature.

Feature overrides seem to be explicitly disabled in the editor by this code:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5df8eae86292303fefe2d412fb8c04126e7ebe87/main/main.cpp#L1311-L1314

I'm not sure why that's needed. We discussed this on RC and I'm not convinced this solves an actual problem:
```
[Akien] reduz: Do you remember why feature overrides are disabled in the editor? https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/main/main.cpp#L1314
[Akien] We've started using the `.editor` feature override for some project settings and it seems like it's actually not working because of this.
[reduz] Akien: So you can actually edit the value and not have the override change things for you
[reduz] Also the overrides only work on load. I need to do some refactoring of how it works so its done on the fly.
[KoBeWi] but the tags can't be modified on the fly, so why? 🤔
[Akien] What kind of edited value would be problematic if it impacts the editor? For example if you add a `.pc` override, wouldn't you expect it to impact the editor? (can be after restart, that's fine)
```

Needs testing IMO.

Here's a list of existing feature overrides which could be relevant for the editor and are currently not respected:

### `editor`

These should apply.
```
$ rg "GLOBAL_DEF.*\.editor"
core/config/project_settings.cpp
1202:   GLOBAL_DEF("display/window/energy_saving/keep_screen_on.editor", false);

main/main.cpp
621:    GLOBAL_DEF("debug/settings/crash_handler/message.editor",
```

### `pc`

This one is debatable, not sure where editor instance logs would go.
```
$ rg "GLOBAL_DEF.*\.pc"
main/main.cpp
1338:   GLOBAL_DEF("debug/file_logging/enable_file_logging.pc", true);
```

### `mobile`

These would be relevant for the Android editor. Currently it will use desktop-optimized settings so it's much more demanding than regular Android exports and might crash GPUs.
```
$ rg "GLOBAL_DEF.*\.mobile"
scene/main/scene_tree.cpp
1473:   GLOBAL_DEF("rendering/shadows/positional_shadow/atlas_size.mobile", 2048);

servers/rendering_server.cpp
2842:   GLOBAL_DEF("rendering/shadows/directional_shadow/size.mobile", 2048);
2845:   GLOBAL_DEF("rendering/shadows/directional_shadow/soft_shadow_filter_quality.mobile", 0);
2850:   GLOBAL_DEF("rendering/shadows/positional_shadow/soft_shadow_filter_quality.mobile", 0);
2856:   GLOBAL_DEF_RST_BASIC("rendering/vulkan/rendering/back_end.mobile", 1);
2876:   GLOBAL_DEF("rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/texture_array_reflections.mobile", false);
2878:   GLOBAL_DEF("rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/ggx_samples.mobile", 16);
2881:   GLOBAL_DEF("rendering/reflections/reflection_atlas/reflection_size.mobile", 128);
2890:   GLOBAL_DEF("rendering/shading/overrides/force_vertex_shading.mobile", true);
2892:   GLOBAL_DEF("rendering/shading/overrides/force_lambert_over_burley.mobile", true);
2971:   GLOBAL_DEF("rendering/environment/glow/upscale_mode.mobile", 0);
```

### `debug`

To be assessed.
```
$ rg "GLOBAL_DEF.*\.debug"
main/main.cpp
617:    GLOBAL_DEF_RST("application/run/flush_stdout_on_print.debug", true);
```

### `web`

Should be used for the Web editor:
```
$ rg "GLOBAL_DEF.*\.web"
servers/audio_server.cpp
188:    GLOBAL_DEF_RST("audio/driver/mix_rate.web", 0); // Safer default output_latency for web (use browser default).
190:    GLOBAL_DEF_RST("audio/driver/output_latency.web", 50); // Safer default output_latency for web.
```

### `windows`

```
$ rg "GLOBAL_DEF.*\.windows"
main/main.cpp
1780:           GLOBAL_DEF_RST_NOVAL("input_devices/pen_tablet/driver.windows", "");
```

comments: Note that if this is addressed, it will remove the ability to define project settings that only apply within the editor (e.g. as requested in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/69528). I suppose this would have to be added another way, such as a `editor_hint` feature tag (as opposed to `editor` which is for editor *binaries*).

review_comments:
Reading this more in depth for the first time - it supports more than one feature override for a given property name? i.e. `keep_screen_on.macos.windows` works to override for both `macos` and `windows`?

I'm not sure we ever use or test this if so, which might mean it could be buggy in some places.
No idea, it seems it always did, I don't mind leaving it there since there is no harm I guess. It should definitely not be buggy, though since it relies on `split()` for everything.

It's not a new issue but it's worth noting that it's possible to have multiple feature overrides which are valid (e.g. `debug` and `pc`, or `mobile` and `android`), and it's not necessarily clear to the user / engine developers which one will be applied.

Just food for thought, I don't think we should change this behavior now, but it can lead to weird issues further down the road (especially if which one ends up first in the `features_overrides` vector is non deterministic.

For now this is deterministic and still depends entirely of the order in which they are defined, but the inspector shows them alphabetically. This would need some changes in the Project Settings editor to detect overrides in the property list and sort them properly, as well as the ability to change their priority.

As this is not new, I would leave it like this for 4.1, but the code in ProjectSettings would need no change currently.
